en\u0000De fleste AI-produkter er avheng: Most AI products rely on an account, a remote server, and an online connection. It is practical, but it also means that the user's workflow is closely linked to the provider's model, pricing model, API and privacy choices.

en\u0000De fleste bedrifter automatisere: Most companies automate too late, not too early — because the manual routines "work well enough" until suddenly they don't: the team grows, the volume increases, or someone quits and takes all the knowledge of how things "are usually done" with them. Here are five concrete signs that it's time to look at automation.
en\u0000De fleste bedriftseiere ser på s: Most business owners look at their own website through nostalgic glasses — "SETAEI built it a few years ago, it works fine". The problem is that potential customers don't have the same patience or loyalty. They compare, often unconsciously, to the best websites they've seen recently — which is rarely a competitor in the same industry, but any good website they've visited in the past week. Here are concrete signs that the website is actually losing customers, not just "could be better".
en\u0000De fleste bedriftsnettsider har: Most business websites have both a one-off cost for development and an ongoing cost for hosting, domain and any maintenance. Be skeptical of offers that seem unnaturally cheap on the one-off cost.
en\u0000De fleste bestemmer seg i løpet: Most people decide within seconds whether they trust a company. Clear message, a visual expression that suits the brand, and one obvious next action at the top of the page.
en\u0000De fleste besøkende kommer fra m: Most visitors come from mobile, and a slow site will lose them. All websites are built fast, mobile-friendly and with technical SEO in place from day one, so you don't have to repair it later.
en\u0000De fleste delte ressurser blir d: Most shared resources deteriorate the more people use them: more queues, less bandwidth per person. REALGRAM is deliberately built in the opposite direction.
en\u0000De fleste engasjementene starter: Most engagements start simply: a non-binding conversation about where the company stands technically and commercially, a brief assessment of architecture and priorities, and then an agreement on either a fixed number of hours per month or a specific delivery project (for example, technical due diligence before an investment round).
en\u0000De fleste gründere venter for le: Most entrepreneurs wait too long to bring in technical leadership — not because they don't see the need, but because they're not sure when "too soon" turns into "too late."
en\u0000De fleste norske bedrifter som «: Most Norwegian companies that "get started with AI" start at the wrong end: a large, undefined mandate ("SETAEI must use AI more") without a concrete problem to measure it against. The result is often a long investigation that never ends up in something that is actually in operation. This article goes through the sequence that works in practice — from finding the right first project to actually putting it into live operation.
en\u0000De fleste norske bedriftsnettsid: Most Norwegian business websites get more traffic from mobile than from PC. If the website is slow to load on mobile, a large proportion of visitors leave the page before it has even finished loading - and they never get to see how good the services actually are.
en\u0000De fleste prosjekter begynner me: Most projects begin with one concrete task and grow when the need becomes clear.
en\u0000De fleste prosjekter har én bruk: Most projects have one user interface and one answer to "what does it do". REALGRAM has four but only one answer to why: to make free, robust internet access a thing

en\u0000Den vanligste feilen er å budsje: The most common mistake is to budget only for the development itself, and forget about the operational costs that come afterwards: hosting, third-party services, security updates and further development based on what actual users ask for. A SaaS product is not a one-time delivery — it is a product that must be operated and developed continuously to retain and grow a customer base.
en\u0000Den vanligste feilen hos førsteg: The most common mistake first-time entrepreneurs make isn't a bad idea — it's building too much, too soon, before someone has confirmed that someone will actually pay for it.
en\u0000Den vanligste fellen er å velge: The most common trap is to choose the cheapest offer without checking what is actually included. A website that is cheap to build but slow, poorly structured for search engines, or built on a platform that makes it expensive to make changes later, often ends up costing more overall — either in lost customers because the page can't be found, or in an expensive rebuild a couple of years later.
en\u0000Den vanligste kostnadsfellen er: The most common cost trap is not a high hourly rate — it is building too big before you know that the solution actually solves the problem. Start with a limited pilot project on one specific problem (for example: automating responses to the 20 most common customer inquiries), measure the effect, and expand from there. It also provides a concrete basis for negotiating the price of the next phase, instead of guessing at the scope of a large system from day one.

en\u0000Design er subjektivt, men et par: Design is subjective, but a few things aren't: hard-to-read font sizes, low-resolution images, or a layout that's clearly from another decade. This is unconsciously read as a signal that the company is not active or up-to-date - even though this is not true at all.

en\u0000Det avhenger av hvor grunnleggen: It depends on how fundamental the problems are. If the problem is primarily speed and some text changes, the existing page can often be adjusted. If it is built on an outdated platform, it is often more profitable to build anew.
en\u0000Det avhenger av omfanget, men po: It depends on the scope, but the point of an MVP is that it should take significantly less time than a full-fledged product — typically weeks rather than months.
en\u0000Det avhenger av omfanget. Etter: It depends on the scope. After the validation step, you get a concrete estimate based on what the MVP actually has to prove, not a guess in advance.
en\u0000Det beste førsteprosjektet er kj: The best first project is boring, concrete and easy to measure — not the most ambitious. Look for tasks that are repetitive, take time, and have a clear "before" and "after" you can compare: customer inquiries that are currently answered manually, documents that are read and categorized by hand, or reports that are put together manually every week. The easier it is to say "this took X hours before, Y minutes now", the easier the rest of the process becomes — including getting internal support for the next project.
en\u0000Det du som kunde har mest kontro: What you as a customer have the most control over is also what affects the timeline the most: have content ready — or at least started — before the project starts, agree fixed deadlines for feedback, and determine the scope before the work begins instead of during the process.
